chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: The Lenox Club band under Cliff Jackson and Jeff Blunt
summary: The Lenox Club drew number runners and the Cotton Club's turned-away crowd; the ten-piece band played hard syncopated numbers, with Herb Branch and Edgar Allen on lead trumpet.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And he had one of those heads on him. But now this Lenox Club, it was where the people who wanted to be like -- they had the same bandstand, somewhat, we had a 10-piece band, Cliff Jackson was the band leader. And he had a sock cymbal on his foot. It seems as though the rhythm wasn't moving him or the German was doing so he had the sock cymbal thing. I noticed that. And he was a left-hand piano player, I guess he liked that bass on the back beat.

So I got a job up there. And all the stars would come up there, all the people who had money. The number runners, people who owned houses and were making this big money, they would come up there and spoil it.
Yes, yes. That's right. And a man whose name was Jeff Blunt. And Jeff Blunt was a man--he was a bit deformed and he had the band. So I was up there. Now, I was

using all the techniques I had learned on the horn and I was trying to read, because as I told you that new music, that new stuff we come up with, synchopation, and he had a hard one. And he had a thing called "Willy Williams Weeper," and all this stuff. And at that time Cab hadn't come into view. And another thing was called "Minnie the Moocher" and all these things we were playing --
Yeah, because the music was there.

But he wasn't famous. And I was there. And at first the first trumpet, his name was Herb Branch, Herb Branch was from Boston. He was a great trumpet player, he was a great classical trumpet player. But Herb left and then they had another fellow named Edgar Allen, he was from St. Louis.
